To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) power consumption is not proportional to the computational complexity of a DNN, (ii) power consumption is highly dependent on the specific operations in the network, (iii) power consumption is dependent on the working condition of the device, and (iv) power consumption can be reduced significantly by optimizing the bit-widths of weights and activations, and by optimizing the working conditions

(i) power consumption in neural networks is highly non-uniform, (ii) the most power-hungry operations are not the same for different network architectures, and (iii) a simple power-aware quantization scheme can achieve high accuracy even when working at low power budgets

(1) the power consumption of DNN operations depends on the input values and the network architecture; (2) power consumption of DMM operations is dominated by the number of iterations, and not by the number of operations; (3) the number of iterations can be significantly reduced by using the input values to control the loop iterations; (4) this approach enables to achieve a power-accuracy trade-off at deployment time, while maintaining high accuracy for low-power operation
In summary, our research is concerned with
a fundamental question of DNN design: how to reduce power consumption without sacrificing performance.
the design of power-aware neural networks, which are a crucial component for enabling DNNs in battery-constrained environments.
the fundamental question of how to design DNNs for minimal power consumption, under a given power budget.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PANN is a simple and effective method that allows a network designer to achieve a given accuracy level at a specific power budget.
PANN is a simple yet very effective method for reducing power consumption, with minimal degradation in accuracy.

our method provides the most accurate and efficient power consumption models for DNNs to date, and can be applied to any pre-trained network with minimal overhead, and can even be used to train a new network from scratch.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide the first power consumption model for neural networks, and show that it is possible to design a network that is aware of the power budget of each module, and therefore achieve optimal power consumption.
we provide the first power consumption model for DNNs that takes into account all the arithmetic operations in the network, which enables to achieve optimal low-power DNNs.
PANN enables a power-efficient deployment of neural networks, while maintaining high accuracy, and without requiring any re-training.
The main takeaway from our work is that
power-aware neural networks can be achieved by simple modifications to the existing training pipeline, without any need for new training algorithms.
the power consumed by each network operation can be accurately predicted and used to optimize power consumption.
the power consumption of a neural network is not a black box.
